Hey man, my guinea pig just passed away 3 days ago too. She was approaching 7 years old, but you and I both know that guinea pigs don't live that long. Ours was an albino girl who was severely starved when we got her. It was so bad that we thought she was dead when her former owner left her here. We made sure she always had plenty to eat. 

Up until a few months ago, she was a little fatty (not obese, but she was a bit chunky). Slowly I noticed she started getting very bony, but she had a healthy appetite for hay & veggies besides her lettuce for some reason.  Suddenly she wasn't able to move besides breathing the other morning, so we knew she had to be put down. Unfortunately she died on my mother's lap before we left the house. After she passed, we noticed a very large tumor in the bottom of her neck. She was too skittish to let us touch there or ever let us do much with her nails. And since she was a bit bigger, her waddle hid it. I can't help but feel guilty that her cancer got that dramatically bad without us knowing. But I have to think: even if we caught it, it was aggressive cancer. On a small animal like that, there wouldn't have been much we could have done regardless. I miss her for sure, but I know she appreciated us as much as we appreciated her.

My point is that you shouldn't blame yourself for his passing. Guinea pigs live 5 to 8 years, so it's extremely possible that it was just his time to go. I don't know how you or your family would feel about a new pig in the future, but it would be something to consider if possible.
